audit.why: Pantheon L1, Skill L2, Singed L3 and 4-5, Pantheon L6, Singed both item stages — content win and full phases already agree, and it matches the mirror at audits/top/pantheon__singed.json. His early lead decays into a drain-tank he cannot kill.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns was template filler — 'track it before every engage', no numbers.
audit.why: Shield Vault is 13/12/11/10/9s, Aegis Assault 22/21/20/19/18s, Comet Spear 11/10.25/9.5/8.75/8s, Grand Starfall 180/165/150s. Aegis Assault's 22s at rank 1 is the longest gap in his kit and the real all-in window.
audit.corrected: Real rank-1 numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns and tied to what each one gates.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were absent: Mega Adhesive grounds Shield Vault (and Grand Starfall), and Fling cancels Aegis Assault.
audit.why: Riot: Shield Vault 'Pantheon dashes to a target' and Grand Starfall 'leaps into the air' — both carry the dash flag, and Singed's Mega Adhesive grounding 'shuts off enemy dashes'. Aegis Assault is flagged channel, 'interruptible — any CC cancels it', and Fling is a knockup. So glue denies his engage and Fling ends his defensive window; neither was on the page.
audit.corrected: Written into whys[3], mid, wants.you[1], breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[2] and dontsFull[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: The page invents a Pantheon passive called 'Aegis of Zeonia' that 'blocks one auto per engagement window' — named in spikes[2] and mid, referenced again in whys[2] and whys[3].
audit.why: Pantheon's passive is Mortal Will: 'Every few spells or attacks, Pantheon's next spell is empowered.' It does not block autos. The advice built on it ('avoid extended auto-trade sequences') was advice against a mechanic that does not exist. The real front-facing damage block is Aegis Assault, his E.
audit.corrected: Fabricated passive removed from all four strings; Mortal Will and Aegis Assault named correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] read 'Sit low for his W execute' — Shield Vault is a dash-stun, not an execute; the paired description was unrelated template text.
audit.why: No ability in Pantheon's kit executes. Calling Shield Vault an execute teaches the wrong health threshold.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are the proxy window: hard-shove toward his tower, run behind it, and let him choose between following you (and taking Poison Trail damage while you Fling him away) or missing two waves of gold. His passive Aegis of Zeonia blocks one auto per engagement window, so avoid extended auto-trade sequences and instead keep moving — Noxious Slipstream gives you the speed to stay ahead of his chase. At level 6, Insanity Potion changes the equation: the stat dump makes his Q no longer lethal in one combo, and you can begin running at him directly. Ghost on the same cooldown means he cannot run you down; now you run at him, drop Mega Adhesive to root him at the edge of poison range, and Fling him back into the cloud. He still has Grand Starfall to escape the side lane, but he has to use it reactively rather than proactively.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are the proxy window: hard-shove toward his tower, run behind it, and let him choose between following you (and taking Poison Trail damage while you Fling him away) or missing two waves of gold. Mega Adhesive is the reason he cannot commit — the glue grounds Shield Vault, his only gap-closer, so drop it on his step-up rather than on the wave. Aegis Assault is a channel: if he sets the shield, Fling knocks him up and cancels it outright, so hold your E for that instead of spending it on chip. At level 6, Insanity Potion changes the equation: the stat dump makes his Q no longer lethal in one combo, and you can begin running at him directly. Ghost on the same cooldown means he cannot run you down; now you run at him, glue him at the edge of poison range, and Fling him back into the cloud. He still has Grand Starfall to escape, but reactively rather than proactively.
